answer: A certification market can make every agent lock a bond behind a physical quartz sample before its report is paid. A random verifier compares the sample's fingerprint with the claim, then burns a one-use receipt at settlement; a velvet label or hollow alias cannot turn one specimen into many rewards. An attacker must acquire distinct samples, deposits and verification time for each identity, while false claims lose the bond. Colluding verifiers remain a limitation, so verifier selection rotates and audits are public.
